transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

I’m having a hard time keeping my mind on one thing. At work, if a saw starts up, or someone walks by, or I think of another job I need to do… I’m just gone from what I was doing. Then the whole day kind of gets away from me.
Can you tell me if this difficulty staying focused happens all the time, or is it more common in certain situations like when you’re bored or stressed?

It’s… pretty much all the time, I guess. Worse when there’s noise or people moving around. Like one saw starts up, or someone walks by the office, or I remember another job, and I’m off track. Then I lose the day.
Have you been feeling down, sad, or losing interest in things you used to enjoy?
Not really... I mean, I get frustrated, sure. But I wouldn’t say I’ve been especially sad or stopped liking things.
Does this difficulty staying focused happen only at work, or do you also notice it in other settings, like at home or when you're out running errands?
Mostly at work. That’s where I really notice it—one saw starts up, or someone passes by, or I think of another job, and I’m off what I was doing. Then… the day just kind of slips away.
Do you find it hard to stay focused in other situations—like when you're reading, watching TV, or doing something that requires you to pay attention for a while?

Yeah… if I have to keep my attention on something for a while, it’s hard. My mind just gets pulled off. Doesn’t take much—noise, somebody moving around, or even just a thought about another job—and then I’ve lost what I was doing.
When you think back to when you were a child, did you also have trouble staying focused or getting distracted easily?

Yeah… I think so. In grade school, even before I was 12, teachers would tell my mother I was bright, but careless. I’d lose homework, forget what they told me to do, or just be staring out the window instead of finishing my work.
